hero.alt: Green illustration with the title Does Vomiting Break Wudu

sources.title: Quran 5:6 (Surah Al-Ma'idah), Quran.com
sources.supports: Commands wudu before prayer and names relieving oneself; vomit is not mentioned in the verse.

sources.title: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 87, Wudu for vomit and nosebleeds, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Abu ad-Darda narration that the Prophet vomited and performed wudu, graded hasan; Tirmidhi lists Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq for wudu and Malik and Shafi'i against.

sources.title: Would I have to repeat my wudhu if I broke my Nafl Salah, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: Hanafi list of eight nullifiers of wudu including vomiting in mouthful.

sources.title: Dealing With Waswasah Regarding Najasah And The Ruling On A Mouthful Of Vomit, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: Defines a mouthful as what the mouth closes on only with difficulty or what prevents speech, measured by the person's own mouth, child or adult; mouthful is najis; certainty is not lifted by doubt.

sources.title: Vomiting and ablution, fatwa 7861, Egypt's Dar al-Ifta
sources.supports: Vomiting does not nullify ablution but is impurity requiring rinsing the mouth and washing what was soiled before prayer.

sources.title: Ruling On Making Iqtida' Of An Imam When His Actions Differ From One's Own Madhhab, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: Names wudu after vomiting among matters needing caution because they are obligations in some madhhabs and not others.

review.notes: Re-read each retrieved page text in this run (captured 2026-10-23): Quran 5:6, Tirmidhi 87, Darul Ifta Birmingham nullifier list, mouthful definition and iqtida fatwas, and Dar al-Ifta fatwa 7861. Article presents the Hanafi mouthful view and the Maliki/Shafi'i view as recorded by Tirmidhi without declaring one universal; Hanbali position stated only as Tirmidhi names Ahmad. sunnah.com ibnmajah 1221 returned 403 and was not used; islamqa is not an approved domain and was not used. claim_checks.claim: The Prophet vomited and then performed wudu, confirmed by Thawban, graded hasan
claim_checks.explanation: Tirmidhi 87 English and Arabic text state he vomited and performed wudu; grade shown as Hasan (Darussalam).

claim_checks.claim: Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq held wudu after vomiting; Malik and Shafi'i did not
claim_checks.explanation: Tirmidhi's Arabic commentary under hadith 87 names these scholars for each position.

claim_checks.claim: In the Hanafi school vomiting a mouthful nullifies wudu
claim_checks.explanation: Darul Ifta Birmingham lists "Vomiting in mouthful" as the third of eight nullifiers.

claim_checks.claim: A mouthful is what the mouth closes on only with difficulty or prevents speech, judged by the person's own mouth
claim_checks.explanation: The fatwa defines the limit of a mouthful in these terms and applies it to adults and children alike.

claim_checks.claim: Vomiting does not nullify ablution but vomit must be rinsed and washed off before prayer
claim_checks.explanation: Dar al-Ifta fatwa 7861 answer states exactly this.

claim_checks.claim: Wudu after vomiting is a matter of caution because it is obligatory in some schools only
claim_checks.explanation: The iqtida fatwa lists performing wudu after vomiting among neglected matters where caution is needed across madhhabs.

claim_checks.claim: The Quranic wudu verse mentions relieving oneself and does not mention vomit
claim_checks.explanation: Retrieved verse text and translation of 5:6 list relieving oneself and intimacy, not vomit.
